source.title: Champions League Performance Insight: Arsenal's right-sided overload — clip 2

situation.outcome: Arsenal exploit a 5v4; Timber runs behind and Martinelli finishes across the goal
situation.human_observation: Per UEFA's technical analysis unit, this clip shows the build-up to Arsenal's first goal, starting with a 5v4 overload Arsenal create on the right. Declan Rice creates space by deliberately avoiding movement toward the ball, instead positioning himself to exploit gaps. Martin Ødegaard then plays a precise pass to Rice's right foot, set up so Rice needs only one touch before delivering a through ball, timed perfectly for Jurriën Timber's run in behind. Gabriel Martinelli cuts across from the back post to attack the five-metre box and score the goal.
situation.priority_problem: How to synchronise a numerical overload (5v4) on one side of the pitch with a receiving player's positioning discipline (avoiding the ball to hold space), a precisely weighted one-touch setup pass, a timed run in behind, and a supporting run across the box to convert the resulting chance.
visible_evidence: Arsenal establish a 5v4 numerical overload on the right side of the pitch.
Declan Rice deliberately avoids moving toward the ball, instead holding a position that exploits space/gaps in the defensive structure.
Martin Ødegaard plays a pass specifically weighted and directed to Rice's right foot.
This pass placement allows Rice to play a first-time (one-touch) through ball rather than needing to control it first.
Rice's through ball is timed perfectly for Jurriën Timber's run in behind the defence.
Gabriel Martinelli makes a run cutting across from the back post to attack the five-metre box.
Martinelli finishes the move to score the goal.

coaching.objective: Combine a numerical overload on one side of the pitch with disciplined off-ball positioning, a precisely weighted one-touch setup pass, and synchronised timed runs (one in behind, one across the box) to convert a created overload into a goal.
coaching.practice_design: Overload-to-finish practice (e.g. 5v4 in a wide channel progressing to goal): one player is coached specifically to hold a position away from the ball, reading gaps rather than checking to receive, to stay available for a one-touch lay-off. A supplying player rehearses playing accurately weighted passes to the receiving player's stronger foot so a first-time through ball is possible without a controlling touch. A third player times a run in behind off that through ball, while a fourth player rehearses a supporting run across the face of goal (back post to five-metre box) to arrive for the finish. Progress from unopposed shape work to a defending back four to replicate the numerical overload being exploited.
success_cues: Attacking side establishes a genuine numerical overload (more attackers than defenders) in the working area before the key pass.
The link player holds position intelligently rather than checking to the ball, staying available for a one-touch pass.
Setup pass is weighted and directed to the receiving player's stronger foot, enabling an immediate one-touch release.
The through ball is timed precisely for the runner's break in behind, neither too early nor too late.
A supporting player arrives across the box (e.g. back post to five-metre area) in time to convert the resulting chance.
